- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply a 10–15 day moving average to dampen noise and align with longer-term trend.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25), model often drifts toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 10-day rolling average of past 30 days.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust subsequent days downward if sentiment remains flat or negative.
